function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have direct access to your network connection, so I can’t tell you your current download/upload speeds myself. Here’s how you can find out: | Method | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **Web browser** | Visit (or ). Click “Go” and wait for the test to finish. | | **Command line (Windows)** | Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and run:
`powershell -Command "(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py', 'speedtest.py'); python speedtest.py"`
*(Requires Python installed.)* | | **Command line (Linux/macOS)** | Install `speedtest-cli` (`sudo apt install speedtest-cli` on Debian/Ubuntu, `brew install speedtest-cli` on macOS) and run:
`speedtest-cli --simple` | | **Mobile app** | Download the official Speedtest app from Google Play Store or Apple App Store and tap “Go”. | If you want me to help you interpret the results or troubleshoot slow speeds, just paste the numbers (download, upload, ping) and let me know what you’re aiming for!
